findings.title: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key (PSK) Vulnerable to Offline Dictionary Attack
findings.subject: SSID: CipherGuard-HQ-Secure (WPA2-Personal)
findings.detail: WPA2 4-Way Handshake allows passive adversaries recording the handshake to execute offline dictionary and brute-force attacks against the pre-shared key (PMK/PTK).
findings.remediation: Enable WPA3-Personal (SAE - Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) with Protected Management Frames (PMF / 802.11w) on your router.

findings.title: Wi-Fi Key Exchange Post-Quantum Susceptibility
findings.subject: WPA2/WPA3 Key Derivation
findings.detail: WPA2 (PBKDF2/SHA1) and WPA3 (ECC Dragonfly P-256) rely on classical cryptography. A recorded Wi-Fi capture can eventually be broken if decrypted by a Cryptanalytically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC) or via pre-shared key recovery.
findings.remediation: Layer IPsec (RFC 9370 post-quantum hybrid KEM) or WireGuard over sensitive Wi-Fi connections.

summary: Connected to 'CipherGuard-HQ-Secure' on 5 GHz (Channel 52). Security: WPA2-Personal / CCMP with 87% signal. Score: 85/100 (Grade B).
quantum_risk: Standard Classical (ECC/RSA Handshake at Risk to CRQC)

findings.title: Direct Physical Egress (No Virtual VPN Tunnel)
findings.subject: Egress: Direct to ISP (Udupi Fastnet Private Limited)
findings.detail: Device network traffic egresses directly through the local Wi-Fi router to the public ISP without an outer IPsec or WireGuard protective tunnel. Local network administrators and upstream ISPs can inspect unencrypted transport metadata and SNI hostnames.
findings.remediation: For sensitive remote access or untrusted networks, establish an IPsec (RFC 4301) or WireGuard tunnel.
